description: The figure contains two side-by-side vertical bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement measured by Fleiss Kappa as a function of sample-level ambiguity metrics. In the left chart, the horizontal axis lists Ambiguity Std categories (labeled 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94) in increasing order, and the vertical axis is labeled “Fleiss Kappa” on a linear scale spanning roughly 0.0 to 0.9 with evenly spaced tick marks (about 0.2 increments); four solid blue bars are shown with numeric annotations above them: Ambiguity Std 0.0 has a dark teal bar at approximately 0.88, 0.47 has a medium blue bar at 0.46, 0.82 has a light blue bar at 0.03, and 0.94 has a brighter blue bar at 0.24. In the right chart, the horizontal axis lists Max Ambiguity categories (1, 2, 3) in increasing order, and the vertical axis is again labeled “Fleiss Kappa” with the same linear scaling and approximate range; three solid blue bars with value labels are shown: Max Ambiguity 1 has a dark teal bar at 0.89, Max Ambiguity 2 has a medium blue bar at 0.46, and Max Ambiguity 3 has a brighter blue bar at 0.23. No legend is present, the bars are not stacked or grouped beyond being separate categories, and the only visual emphasis is the numeric value annotations placed above each bar.
caption_used: Inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, compared to sample-level ambiguity metrics, including standard deviation and maximum ambiguity values. The left bar chart illustrates a marked decline in Fleiss Kappa as Ambiguity Std increases, with values dropping precipitously from approximately 0.88 at an Ambiguity Std of 0.0 to 0.03 at 0.82, before stabilizing at 0.31 for the highest ambiguity category (0.94). The right bar chart demonstrates a similar but less consistent trend for Max Ambiguity, where Fleiss Kappa starts at 0.89 for the lowest ambiguity category (1), then declines sharply to 0.46 at Max Ambiguity of 2, and further collapses to 0.23 at the highest ambiguity level (3). Notably, the rate of decline in inter-annotator agreement is more pronounced between the first and second categories of Ambiguity Std than between corresponding categories of Max Ambiguity, suggesting a stronger sensitivity to variability in ambiguity than to its absolute magnitude.
